subtasks.text: Technical Description of the Problem: Develop a multimodal geospatial foundation model that predicts spatial crop yield from heterogeneous field-level data layers collected at different spatial and temporal resolutions. For each agricultural field, a ground-truth yield map is available from harvested yield-monitor data. The model receives a variable set of geospatial inputs that may include elevation and terrain derivatives, soil properties, crop-history layers, weather and climate time series, soil moisture, radar imagery, optical satellite imagery, aerial imagery, and other remote-sensing or management-related data. The objective is to learn a reusable field representation that can support yield-map prediction as the primary task while also enabling additional agricultural prediction heads.

subtasks.text: Yield Prediction Head: The primary supervised task is dense yield-map prediction. Given the multimodal field representation, a spatial decoder should reconstruct yield at the desired output grid. The decoder may use transformer queries, convolutional upsampling, feature pyramids, or another spatial decoding architecture. Predictions should preserve within-field spatial variability rather than producing only a field-average yield. Training targets are observed yield maps aligned to the corresponding field geometry.
subtasks.title: Yield Prediction Head

subtasks.text: Foundation-Model Design: The central transformer should not be tied exclusively to yield prediction. Build the system as a shared backbone with multiple task-specific heads. The initial head predicts yield maps, while future heads may support outcomes such as field-average yield, crop-stress detection, soil-property inference, management-zone segmentation, moisture estimation, anomaly detection, or other precision-agriculture tasks. New heads should be attachable without redesigning individual modality encoders.
subtasks.title: Foundation-Model Design

subtasks.text: Missing-Modality Robustness: The model must operate when only a subset of inputs is available. Different fields and years may lack specific satellite acquisitions, weather variables, soil datasets, or high-resolution imagery. The architecture should therefore treat modalities as optional rather than assuming a fixed input tensor. Use explicit modality tokens and masks, and train with modality dropout so that random input sources are removed during training. Investigate whether a learned missing-modality token, masked-modality modeling, or cross-modal reconstruction objectives improve robustness. Evaluate performance as progressively more modalities are removed and determine which combinations provide the most predictive information.
subtasks.title: Missing-Modality Robustness

subtasks.text: Pretraining: In addition to supervised yield-map training, investigate self-supervised and multimodal pretraining so that the backbone learns general representations from fields without yield maps. Candidate objectives include masked spatial-token reconstruction, masked modality prediction, temporal reconstruction, contrastive alignment between modalities covering the same field, cross-modal prediction, and reconstruction of one sensor from representations learned from others. Pretrained modality encoders may initially be frozen and later selectively fine-tuned. Compare frozen, partially fine-tuned, and fully fine-tuned configurations.
subtasks.title: Pretraining

subtasks.text: Data Organization: Treat each field-year pair as one multimodal sample. Inputs may include static layers such as DEM, terrain, and soil; low-frequency historical variables such as crop history; temporal environmental observations such as weather, precipitation, and soil moisture; and multitemporal remote sensing such as Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, NAIP, PlanetScope, or comparable sources. All layers must be geographically registered to the same field, but they need not be resampled to the same native resolution before encoding.
subtasks.title: Data Organization

subtasks.text: Training Protocol: Split data at the field level, and where possible evaluate geographically and temporally separated test sets to avoid spatial leakage. Test generalization to unseen fields, regions, years, crop conditions, and combinations of missing modalities. Compare the multimodal transformer against strong baselines including yield prediction from individual modalities, early fusion after raster resampling, late fusion of independently trained encoders, CNN-based multimodal models, and simpler ensemble approaches.
subtasks.title: Training Protocol

subtasks.text: Evaluation: Evaluate dense prediction using RMSE, MAE, R², normalized RMSE, spatial correlation, and field-level yield error. Also evaluate preservation of spatial yield patterns, particularly low- and high-yield zones. Report performance for complete-input and partial-input conditions. Perform modality ablations to measure the marginal contribution of terrain, soil, weather, moisture, optical imagery, SAR, and other sources. Measure how much each additional modality improves predictions and whether its usefulness varies geographically or temporally.
subtasks.title: Evaluation

subtasks.text: Interpretability: Provide attention, attribution, or modality-importance analyses showing which sources and spatial regions influence predictions. Determine whether the model learns physically meaningful relationships among terrain, soil, moisture, vegetation condition, weather, and yield rather than relying primarily on one dominant imagery source.
subtasks.title: Interpretability

subtasks.text: Model Output and Deliverables: Deliver a modular multimodal architecture containing dedicated modality encoders, a shared fusion transformer, a dense yield-map decoder, support for optional and missing modalities, and an extensible multi-head output interface. Deliver comparisons of encoder strategies, fusion mechanisms, native-resolution versus resampled processing, frozen versus fine-tuned pretrained encoders, and robustness under missing-data conditions.
